scope: Read-only diagnosis and comparison; business code and production unchanged
shared_findings: Prompt and validator use different summary length wording
Length repair has no measured count or exact target
Cold resume loses failed metadata and original validation error
December temporal expressions can be rejected despite explicit source wording
Daily and weekly frozen cards and cross-run quota protection worked in the observed runs

decisions.conclusion: Use one non-whitespace Unicode-character metric; retain the existing 250 hard cap and report measured length.

Three real summaries can retain their first two complete sentences at 171/171/188 characters and pass full writing validation with all 20 cards unchanged. This removes summary topics; editorial policy acceptance is required before automatic use.
The cold-resume context loss is real. A new repair-draft stage is not necessary solely for overlength; consider bound unvalidated context later for content repairs.

One correction per process is existing policy. Do not globally remove its guard; any later adjustment must stay within stage request/time limits and distinguish writer local repair from editor/full correction/permanent errors.
Not established as the cause. The normal merge path preserves prior good cards, verified progressively from 1 to 3.
Bound the December fix to actual temporal contexts. annual/year-ending to 12 months is semantically plausible but unsupported by current literal-number policy, not proof of invented facts.

current_weekly_recovery.method: After explicit acceptance and publication authorization, assemble validated metadata from saved sentences under the matching old rules, fully validate, then use existing ready/publish verification. Do not clear quota or modify old rules fingerprints.
